fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it.

fabric-api-lookup-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (unchanged from upstream) because its transfer API builds on it.

fabric-biome-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API and biome source mixins, with biome modifications applied as a NeoForge biome modifier (upstream replaces biome fields NeoForge keeps private and no longer reads, and its weather changes read a field NeoForge's coremod keeps private).

fabric-block-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's block hooks (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); NeoForge's own chunk-section air check is kept.

fabric-client-gametest-api-v1.reason: development-time test framework, not needed to play

fabric-content-registries-v0.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's registries and mixins, with NeoForge's data maps backed by them where an entry is missing; entity swimming, jumping, drowning and boat floating in Fabric-registered fluids are not applied (NeoForge rewrote that code).

fabric-crash-report-info-v1.reason: NeoForge already lists every mod in crash reports; nothing else to provide.

fabric-data-generation-api-v1.reason: Mods' runtime code references its classes (Wover's entrypoints load its tag providers); its hooks act only when the fabric-api.datagen property is set. Its tag appender mixins add removal methods NeoForge's own tag appenders already declare, so they are left out: removing entries through a Fabric tag builder doesn't work in data generation.

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: DataFixerUpper is a library NeoForge loads without mixin support, so the safety net for worlds that reference a removed modded dimension is not available.

fabric-entity-events-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's entity events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); elytra and most sleep events are not fired.

fabric-events-interaction-v0.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's interaction events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); attack entity callbacks get no hit result, and client-side cancelled interactions still reach the server.

fabric-gametest-api-v1.reason: development-time test framework, not needed to play

fabric-item-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's item hooks and events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); equipment slot providers get no entity.

fabric-lifecycle-events-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches).

fabric-loot-api-v3.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's builder and drop mixins as they are, its loading hook replaced by NeoForge's LootTableLoadEvent (upstream's conflicts with NeoForge's loot loading).

fabric-menu-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's menu opening data: extended menus send their opening data the way NeoForge mods' menus do (upstream's mixins target the openMenu NeoForge replaced).

fabric-model-loading-api-v1.reason: Model loading plugins, extra models (added to the models NeoForge's own overload of the discovery resolves) and model modifiers work. Fabric's custom model formats (fabric:type in model and blockstate files) work through NeoForge's parsers, next to NeoForge's own (loader, type): upstream's hooks into vanilla's parsers are left out, because NeoForge's model file deserializer takes precedence over upstream's and upstream's blockstate codec would replace NeoForge's.

fabric-networking-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's payload system (login queries are not supported).

fabric-object-builder-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's registration events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches); custom minecart comparator logic is not used by detector rails.

fabric-particles-v1.reason: NeoForge builds sprint and fall particles with their block position already; upstream's mixins add it to the vanilla constructor NeoForge no longer calls.

fabric-recipe-api-v1.reason: NeoForge already gives Ingredient a hashCode, which upstream's mixin would replace.

fabric-registry-sync-v0.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's registries, which already sync ids to clients (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches).

fabric-renderer-api-v1.reason: Upstream loads with Indigo as the renderer, so meshes and quad emitters work, and NeoForge keeps drawing blocks: upstream's hooks that send every block in the world, every moving block and every breaking overlay through Fabric's renderer are left out. Fabricated sends only the blocks whose model is a Fabric model (its own emitQuads, or a vanilla multipart or weighted model with one among its parts) through it instead, in the world, as moving blocks and in the breaking overlay, while every other block keeps NeoForge's renderer. Block outlines, and the glow outline of a moving block, still come from a model's parts as NeoForge sees them. NeoForge already declares createGeometryKey and particleMaterial on vanilla's models with Fabric's signatures, so upstream's copies are left out (BlockStateModel, which inherits both defaults of each, gets NeoForge's declared as a default method bridge). Its emitQuads defaults are NeoForge-aware, as in Forgified Fabric API: a model without its own collects its parts with the level, so NeoForge models keep their level and model data when Fabric's renderer draws them (inside a Fabric model, or every model under a renderer such as Sodium), and parts keep NeoForge's ambient occlusion. NeoForge moved block model baking into its own overload of SimpleModelWrapper.bake, which upstream's mesh check doesn't reach, so a mesh model using sprites from outside the block atlas is not rejected.

fabric-rendering-fluids-v1.reason: NeoForge decides where fluids show their overlay texture with BlockState.shouldDisplayFluidOverlay instead of the check upstream modifies, so blocks marked transparent through FluidRenderingRegistry.setBlockTransparency keep NeoForge's behavior. Custom fluid renderers work.

fabric-rendering-v1.reason: NeoForge draws the HUD in layers: Fabricated runs Fabric's HUD elements from NeoForge's vanilla layers instead of upstream's HUD mixin. Picture-in-picture renderers registered with Fabric are not used (NeoForge rebuilt that renderer), and the debug options screen keeps vanilla's sorting and search. Render pipeline snippets don't carry Fabric's GUI draw mode flag (NeoForge added a field to them); pipelines do.

fabric-resource-conditions-api-v1.reason: NeoForge decides whether data files and registry entries load with its own conditions: Fabricated evaluates fabric:load_conditions there, with upstream's conditions, instead of upstream's mixins on the code NeoForge rewrote.

fabric-resource-loader-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated on NeoForge's reload-listener and pack-finder events (upstream's mixins conflict with NeoForge's patches).

fabric-screen-api-v1.reason: NeoForge draws screens through its own hook: Fabricated fires the before/after extract events from NeoForge's screen render events instead of upstream's wrapper.

fabric-sound-api-v1.reason: NeoForge asks each sound instance for its audio stream: Fabricated uses a Fabric sound instance's own stream there instead of upstream's redirect.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: NeoForge tag files already have a remove list, which NeoForge applies: Fabricated adds fabric:remove entries to it instead of upstream's own removal handling.

fabric-transfer-api-v1.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's API and mixins, with the container mixins reworked onto NeoForge's transaction-aware setItem; NeoForge hoppers don't see Fabric-only storages yet.
